text:
anya: quick follow-up from the RFC review — we talked about a quarantine window for handbacks to avoid immediate reclaims. i'm trying to sketch the simpler epoch-based alternative and want feedback.

mike: curious — what's the concrete problem we're solving with quarantine vs epoch? can you summarize tradeoffs?

anya: TL;DR: quarantine delays reassigning a prefix for X ms after demote+handback to avoid churn from rapid reclaims during transient spikes. epoch approach would attach an epoch id to residency tokens and require lease advancement to reclaim, so no time-based waiting but extra metadata and stricter fencing semantics.

rajesh: quarantine is simple and low-risk, but it couples correctness to timing heuristics — tricky across heterogeneous tenants. epoch/fence sounds safer for correctness but might increase RPCs for epoch checks.

lukas: also: quarantine interacts badly with soft-demote/backfill path. If we quarantine too long hot tenants suffer. We observed this during the small-tenant experiment last week.

anya: exactly. that's why i'm proposing a hybrid: short quarantine (100-300ms) + lightweight epoch stamps for strong-fence only on contested prefixes. so cheap common case, strong safety on races. thoughts?

mike: hybrid sounds pragmatic. how do we detect "contested" cheaply? add a hot-counter on the prefix entry and escalate when >N attempts within window?

rajesh: we already have recent-access counters for hotkey heuristics. reuse them. if counter spikes during quarantine window => mark contested and issue epoch fence.

lukas: caution: escalation path must be idempotent and observable. ops needs metrics: escalation-rate, mean-latency impact, and extra RPC rate.

anya: good point. proposed metrics: prefix.escalations, prefix.escalation_latency_p50/p95, prefix.quarantine_hits, prefix.epoch_checks. add a boolean tag for tenant tier.

ci-bot: scheduled: rollout canary for 'quarantine+epoch-hybrid' on rig-05 at 2025-06-05T09:00Z. ci-bot:link: https://ci.internal/runs/7890

mike: implementation note: epoch field should be a 64-bit monotonic generation id stored with residency record. reclaim path compares local view vs record and only proceeds if epoch advanced. if we escalate, coordinator increments epoch and broadcasts.

rajesh: how expensive is a coordinator increment broadcast? could we piggyback on existing lease heartbeat messages?

anya: yes. plan: piggyback epoch bumps on existing lease-fencing RPC so no new RPC type for common cases. escalation path triggers the bump and a fast invalidation message.

lukas: testing plan? we need unit tests for multiple races: concurrent handback+reclaim, handback during demote, and cross-node quick-reclaim loops. add a chaos job to repeatedly demote/rehydrate a small set of prefixes.

anya: test matrix: (1) unit race harness, (2) local canary rig with telemetry, (3) cross-rig chaos for 10m, measure 0 visible errors and <2% latency regression for warm reads.

mike: compatibility: older runtimes won't understand epoch bumps. do we need a versioned residency proto?

rajesh: yes — residency proto v2 with optional epoch. fallback: if peer doesn't support epoch, we fall back to quarantine-only for that prefix. mark metric prefix.epoch_peer_mismatch.

anya: decision draft: implement hybrid (short quarantine + on-demand epoch escalation) + proto v2 optional epoch + telemetry. canary next week. anybody object?

lukas: no objection. add a kill-switch flag and 2-minute backout steps in rollout playbook.

mike: one more: ensure eviction policy priority doesn't get inverted by quarantine. hot prefixes should still preempt low-priority tenants. add rule: quarantine does not affect eviction scoring, only assignment timing.

rajesh: ack. i'll sketch the proto change and a sequence diagram for escalation.

anya: thanks. i'll update RFC branch with the hybrid design and the canary checklist. assigned: @rajesh for proto, @mike for scoring rule, @lukas for metrics + playbook. i'll open PR by EOD. :thumbsup:

lukas: thanks — looking forward to the PR.

ci-bot: build passed for branch 'hybrid-epoch-quarantine' (commit abc123)

anya: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/412 — please review.

mike: reviewing now. quick Q in PR about escalation threshold defaults. prefer conservative defaults for canary.

rajesh: i'll add config knobs and notes for tuning per-rig.

anya: perfect. closing the thread for now, will re-open if canary shows issues.
